To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the initial calcification of matrix vesicles is not associated with calcium accumulation within the vesicles, instead it occurs at the outer surface membrane.

the initial calcium deposition occurs at the outer surface of the preodontoblastic cell and that the calcium is then transported into the matrix vesicles and finally into the preodontoblasitic cells, where it is incorporated into the collagen matrix.

matrix vesicles contain only a small amount of calcium, which is not detectable by antimonate precipitation, and that calcium is accumulated on the outer surface of matrix vesicles, and that calcium accumulates in mitochondria and Golgi area during the preodontoblastic stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ultrastructural localization, distribution, and accumulation of calcium in preodontoblast and matrix vesicles of developing rat mola tooth germs during the initial stages of dentinogenesis.
the calcium accumulation and distribution during the initial stages of rat molar tooth germ development.
the localization of calcium in preodontoblast and in the extracellular space during initial stages of rat molar dentinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the calcium accumulation in the precalcification and matrix vesicle calcifying stage is mainly associated with preodontoblast mitochondria, while in the collagen calcification stage calcium is mainly distributed in the Golgi region, secretory granule and lateral intercellicular space of the late preodonto-blasts.

calcium accumulation and precipitation in the preodontblast is a complex and dynamic process, and the calcium is transported and stored in mitochondria and Golgi area, then released to the secretory granules in the Golgi area and transported to the extracellular matrix, finally, the calcium in the secretory granule is released and precipitated on the outer surface of matrix vesicles and the preodontoblastic plasma membrane.
matrix vesicles are involved in calcium transport and mineralization of the extracellular matrix of developing rat molars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the preodontoblastic cell membrane is a major source of calcium for matrix vesicle calcifications and that calcium is transported to the matrix vesicles by a process involving Golgi area, mitochondria and the secretory granules of preodontoblastic cells.

calcium is first stored in preodontoblast mitochondria, subsequently, in the Golgi area, and finally, in matrix vesicles in a sequence which may be related to the maturation and calcification of matrix vesicles.
matrix vesicles are the primary site for the initial mineralization of the developing tooth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium is accumulated in matrix vesicles at a later stage in the development of rat molar tooth.
the initial calcium localization within matrix vesicles is not a prerequisite for their role in mineralization.
matrix vesicles may not be a primary site of calcium accumulation and that the outer surface membrane may play a more important role in calcium accumulation during initial dentin formation.
